text:
Tyler Toffoli is closing in on 1,000 NHL games on his seventh team, and in San Jose he's become the veteran who tells the kids where to stand on the power play. He has 6 goals and 14 points in 24 games, 7 of those points with the man advantage, including a goal and an assist on the power play in Utah last weekend.

His five-on-five game is more complicated. He's down to 13 minutes a night, and the Sharks get only about 47% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on, though that's still better than when he sits. His goals sit right around his chances. He was never fast, and at 34 his skating numbers sit near the bottom of the league; his shot is still above average. That combination explains the role: he's a finisher who needs someone else to carry the puck to him.

Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.4 wins last season, when he scored 19 goals, and he's 58th in the league in our wins added this year. On a young team still learning to win, a Cup winner who scores timely goals matters. We'd watch whether his even-strength minutes keep shrinking.
